title: Fix 'Is a directory' when cat is used on a folder
summary: The cat command prints the text inside a file. A folder has no text to print, so cat stops with the message Is a directory. List the folder to see its files, then read the file you need with cat.

aliases.text: linux cat folder not a file
how to see what is inside a folder in linux
cat Is a directory что значит
это директория а не файл linux
как посмотреть что внутри папки в терминале linux
ls список файлов в папке linux

prerequisites: You have a Linux terminal open
You know the path of the folder you tried to read

steps.explain: cat prints the text of a file. You gave it a folder, which only holds other files, so there is no text to print. List the folder to see what it contains. Folders are shown with a / at the end.

placeholders.name: FOLDER
placeholders.description: Path of the folder you tried to read with cat.

steps.expect: A list of file and folder names, such as hosts and alternatives/. Names ending with / are folders.

alternatives.explain: Show the same list with details: permissions, owner, size and date of each item.

placeholders.name: FOLDER
placeholders.description: Path of the folder you tried to read with cat.

alternatives.expect: One line per item. A line starting with - is a file, and a line starting with d is a folder.

steps.explain: Read one file from the list. Write the folder path, a slash, and the file name, so cat gets the path of the file and not of the folder.

placeholders.name: FOLDER
placeholders.description: Path of the folder that holds the file.

placeholders.name: FILE
placeholders.description: Name of a file inside the folder, taken from the list in the previous step.

steps.expect: The text inside the file appears. No Is a directory message is shown.

verify.expect: The first character of the line is d, which confirms that the path is a folder.
The text of the file is printed, without the Is a directory message.

source.title: cat manual; card written and verified in the lnxhelp sandbox
